manual-eli10.title: 00 / ELI10
manual-eli10.body: A container is an empty div. blocks is the system connected to that div. A block is one individual box inside it.

manual-eli10-steps.title: three things, in order
steps: Create blocks and connect it to that div with blocks.attach(...).
Add one individual block with blocks.add(...).

manual-start.title: 01 / start the system
manual-start.intro: Load the released v0.2.0 build, then attach the system before adding content. setGrid(6, 4) creates six columns and four rows.

manual-finish.title: 02 / add the block
manual-finish.intro: Choose one content value, then pass it to blocks.add(). The three live blocks below show the accepted forms: trusted HTML, one DOM object and a factory that creates a fresh object.

manual-content-object.title: content / object
manual-content-object.caption: 02 / direction
manual-content-object.alt: Black-and-white skatepark with converging concrete ramps, painted lines and a metal rail.

manual-menu.title: 03 / menu actions
manual-menu.intro: The titlebar can show minimize, close, both or neither. The four blocks below are the complete on/off set. A controller can also minimize, restore or remove its own block. Close removes this example; reload the page to restore the full manual.

manual-menu-title.title: title / optional
manual-menu-title.statement: A title is not an id.
manual-menu-title.body: id identifies the block. Add title only when you want visible text in its menu bar; without it, the id stays available to the controls but is not shown.

manual-layout.title: 04 / layout and movement
manual-layout.intro: Set size first, then position. Columns come before rows and coordinates start at 1. Read the current grid size through blocks.columns and blocks.rows. margin reserves empty space inside the field border. With snap and draggable on, drag the titlebar or focus it and use the arrow keys.

manual-layout-small.title: flow / 2 × 2
manual-layout-small.body: Releases the fixed position, not the size.

manual-compact.title: 05 / compact after changes
manual-compact.intro: Use compact() after removing or moving fixed blocks when you want the placed grid to close vertical gaps. It moves fixed blocks upward inside their columns; it does not resize the grid.

manual-appearance.title: 06 / choose an appearance
manual-appearance.intro: Choose one fixed monochrome variant. Regular uses dark ink on paper; inverse exchanges figure and ground. Color and chance come later.

manual-colors.title: 07 / set a color
manual-colors.intro: Set one block color directly. Any valid CSS color can define its border, titlebar and hover frame; the content surface stays neutral.

manual-random.title: 08 / set the chance
manual-random.intro: Chance affects only future blocks added with the random variant. The three left cells change the color share; the three right cells change the inverse share of the monochrome remainder. Values run from 0 to 1.

manual-random-combined.title: color + inverse / 0.5 + 0.5
manual-random-combined.intro: Combine both chances only after reading them separately. In this fixed four-call demonstration, two cells use color, one is regular and one is inverse. Real calls remain random.

reference-adapters.title: 07 / definitions and adapters
reference-adapters.intro: Definitions describe reusable content. Adapters own its mount and cleanup lifecycle.

reference-event.title: 08 / events
reference-event.intro: The field dispatches blocks:reorder after pointer or keyboard reordering and blocks:change after explicit state changes.
reference-event.details: For blocks:reorder, input is pointer or keyboard, mode is grid or flow, and positions are { column, row } or null. For blocks:change, type is compact, minimize, restore or remove; id is one block or null, and ids lists affected blocks.

reference-errors.title: 10 / errors and boundaries
reference-errors.details: Expect errors for invalid or duplicate ids, missing fields, impossible grid positions, overlaps, unknown definitions, incomplete adapters and colorVariation without colors. Catch only errors your interface can recover from.
